I will not start from zero. I have farmed here for 40 years, so I will mostly keep the same pattern that is safest for my land and my pocket. On my 15 mu, I will keep 10 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and 5 mu in cotton. In Quzhou, wheat and maize are still my steady base because I have well irrigation, and with water in hand I can push yield without gambling too much on the weather. Cotton I will keep on a smaller block because it can still make money, but it needs more spraying and more field watching. On fertilizer, I do not like to cut too hard. If I save a few hundred yuan on fertilizer and lose yield, that is a bad deal. Still, I will not throw fertilizer blindly. Wheat gets the heaviest feeding because I want strong tillers and full grain. Maize gets enough nitrogen to carry ear size, but I will not overdo it because too much top growth can waste money. Cotton needs a steadier balance, especially potassium, otherwise the plant looks good but the bolls do not hold as well. For tillage, I will keep the wheat ground in rotary tillage because it fits my labor and timing; after wheat I will put maize in with less disturbance to save time and catch moisture; cotton ground I will plough once so the root zone opens better. On water, I will spend it mainly where it pays: wheat gets the most irrigations, maize gets one key irrigation if rain is short, and cotton gets several smaller irrigations through the critical stages. That is how I will manage risk this year: stable rotation, enough fertilizer, water at the important times, and no fancy changes unless I see a clear gain.
